title: Grade 12 Physics — Modern Physics: Dual Nature, Atoms & Nuclei
description: Photoelectric effect, de Broglie, atomic models, radioactivity
subject: physics

questions.question: The photoelectric effect shows that light behaves as:
options: Packets of energy (photons) — particle nature of light
questions.explanation: Photoelectric effect (Einstein, 1905): light hits a metal surface and ejects electrons. Key features: (1) Below threshold frequency — no emission. (2) Above threshold — instantaneous emission. This proves light is quantised (photons).

questions.question: The energy of a photon with frequency f is:
questions.explanation: E = hf = hc/λ. h = 6.63×10⁻³⁴ J·s. Einstein's photoelectric equation: KE_max = hf − φ (φ = work function = minimum energy to eject an electron). Threshold frequency: f₀ = φ/h.

questions.question: de Broglie wavelength of a particle with momentum p is:
questions.explanation: de Broglie: λ = h/p = h/(mv). Particles (electrons, protons) also have wave nature. Explains quantised atomic orbits (standing wave condition). Electrons in microscopes use very small λ → high resolution.

questions.question: Bohr's model of the atom quantises:
options: The angular momentum of the electron: L = nh/(2π) = nℏ
questions.explanation: Bohr's quantisation condition: angular momentum L = nh/(2π) = nℏ where n = 1, 2, 3... (quantum number). This leads to discrete energy levels: Eₙ = −13.6/n² eV for hydrogen.

questions.question: The energy of the nth level in a hydrogen atom is:
questions.explanation: Eₙ = −13.6/n² eV. Ground state (n=1): E₁ = −13.6 eV. n=2: E₂ = −3.4 eV. Ionisation energy = 13.6 eV. Negative sign = bound state. Photon energy emitted: ΔE = Eᵢ − Eₓ = hf.

questions.question: Alpha decay: ²³⁸₉₂U → ? + α (₂⁴He)
questions.explanation: Alpha decay: mass number decreases by 4, atomic number decreases by 2. ²³⁸₉₂U → ²³⁴₉₀Th + ₂⁴He. ²³⁴₉₀Th = Thorium-234.

questions.question: Beta minus (β⁻) decay involves:
options: Emission of an electron and an antineutrino: n → p + e⁻ + ν̄ₑ
questions.explanation: β⁻ decay: a neutron converts to a proton + electron (β particle) + antineutrino. Atomic number increases by 1; mass number unchanged. β⁺ decay: proton → neutron + positron + neutrino.

questions.question: Nuclear fission is the process in which:
options: Two nuclei combine to form a larger nucleus
A heavy nucleus splits into smaller nuclei + energy (E=mc²)
Gamma rays are emitted from the nucleus
questions.explanation: Fission: heavy nucleus (e.g., ²³⁵U) absorbs a neutron and splits into smaller nuclei + neutrons + huge energy. ²³⁵U + n → ¹⁴¹Ba + ⁹²Kr + 3n + energy. Chain reaction → nuclear reactor/bomb.

questions.question: Mass defect (Δm) of a nucleus is the difference between:
options: Mass of nucleus and mass of protons only
Sum of masses of constituent nucleons and actual nuclear mass: Δm = Zm_p + Nm_n − M
Mass numbers of products and reactants
questions.explanation: Δm = Zm_p + Nm_n − M. This mass difference is converted to binding energy: BE = Δm × c². Greater BE = more stable nucleus. BE per nucleon (binding energy curve) peaks at Fe-56 (most stable).

questions.question: Stopping potential (V₀) in the photoelectric effect is the potential that:
options: Just stops the most energetic photoelectrons (eV₀ = KE_max = hf − φ)
Is equal to the frequency of light
questions.explanation: Stopping potential V₀: the reverse potential needed to stop all photoelectrons. eV₀ = KE_max = hf − φ. V₀ depends on frequency, not intensity. Doubling intensity doubles current but NOT stopping potential.

questions.question: The half-life of a radioactive element is related to the decay constant λ by:
questions.explanation: T₁/₂ = ln2/λ = 0.693/λ. Mean life τ = 1/λ = T₁/₂/0.693. N = N₀e^(−λt) (exponential decay law). Activity A = λN = A₀e^(−λt).

questions.question: The work function of a metal is 2 eV. The threshold frequency is: (h = 6.6×10⁻³⁴ J·s, 1 eV = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ J)
Gamma rays emitted during nuclear decay are:
options: High-energy photons (electromagnetic radiation) from the excited nucleus
questions.explanation: Gamma (γ) rays: high-energy photons (λ ~ 10⁻¹¹ to 10⁻¹⁴ m). They carry no charge and no mass. Emitted when nucleus transitions from excited to ground state. Most penetrating radiation — stopped by thick lead or concrete.

questions.question: Nuclear fusion is the energy source of the Sun. It requires:
options: Very high temperatures (~10⁷ K) and pressures to overcome Coulomb repulsion of nuclei
questions.explanation: Fusion: light nuclei (e.g., H isotopes) fuse into heavier nuclei + energy. In Sun: 4H → ⁴He + energy. Requires 10⁷ K (thermal energy > Coulomb barrier). Fusion releases more energy per kg than fission. Challenge: controlled fusion on Earth.

questions.question: The de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through potential V is:
questions.explanation: eV = ½mv² → p = mv = √(2meV). λ = h/p = h/√(2meV). For V = 100 V: λ ≈ 1.23/√V nm = 0.123 nm (X-ray range — explains electron diffraction).
